extensionAttribute.description: Reports whether the Time Machine destination volume is encrypted.
extensionAttribute.scriptContentsMac:
#!/bin/zsh
# Updated by SecurityShrimp 2026 # Time Machine Encryption Status Extension Attribute # Targets macOS 12 through 26 (Tahoe), Intel and Apple Silicon # CoreStorage (the original "diskutil cs" backend) is dead — macOS uses # APFS for everything now. We use diskutil info -plist on the destination # mount point and read the Encryption status directly.
mount=$(/usr/bin/tmutil destinationinfo 2>/dev/null \ | /usr/bin/awk -F': ' '/Mount Point/ { print $2; exit }')
if [[ -z "$mount" ]]; then if /usr/bin/tmutil destinationinfo 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/grep -q "No destinations configured"; then echo "<result>Backup Not Enabled</result>" else echo "<result>Disk not available</result>" fi exit 0 fi
encrypted=$(/usr/sbin/diskutil info -plist "$mount" 2>/dev/null \ | /usr/bin/plutil -extract Encryption raw - 2>/dev/null)
case "$encrypted" in true|1) echo "<result>Encrypted</result>" ;; false|0) echo "<result>Not Encrypted</result>" ;; *) echo "<result>Unknown</result>" ;; esac
